description: Section taxonomy for AI-drafted transition documentation. Each kind maps to one of the artefacts a manual transition team produces during legacy hand-over: system overview, entry-point map, module catalogue, data dictionary, glossary, interface catalogue, business-rule catalogue, headline diagrams. Risk register and operational runbook are intentionally absent — they need humans who ran the system in production and are not safe to auto-draft. Per ADR-038 each DocSection row carries one of these kinds and rides the DRAFT → IN_REVIEW → SIGNED lifecycle of Spec.

sectionKinds.label: System overview
sectionKinds.description: 2-5 page summary of what the system does in business terms, headline subsystems, key flows. The first page a new engineer reads. Auto-drafted from rolled-up module summaries; SME heavily edits before signing.

fields.name: summary
fields.doc: Plain-English description, 200-1000 words. Markdown allowed (headings, lists, links, mermaid blocks).

fields.name: subsystems
fields.doc: Names of headline subsystems referenced from the overview.

fields.name: citations
fields.doc: Cite the modules / files the overview synthesises from. Drift detection uses these.

sectionKinds.label: Entry-point map
sectionKinds.description: Ranked list of the 10-20 routines that explain 80% of the system. Ranking comes from the migration-plan blast-radius score (Phase 8.0.c) — no LLM judgement needed for the ranking, only for the per-entry justification. Cuts onboarding from weeks to days.

fields.name: entries
fields.doc: Array of { subroutineId, justification, callDepth, blastRadiusScore }. Ordered by rank.

sectionKinds.label: Module catalogue entry
sectionKinds.description: Per-module entry: domain purpose, public surface (entry points), 'you would touch this when…', dependencies, notable risks. Rolls up routine summaries within the module.

fields.name: purpose
fields.doc: Domain-level description, 50-300 words.

fields.name: publicSurface
fields.doc: Names of routines / data items intended for external callers.

fields.name: touchWhen
fields.doc: One sentence: when would an engineer come edit this module?

fields.name: knownRisks
fields.doc: Brittle bits the LLM noticed. SME confirms or removes during review.

sectionKinds.label: Routine summary
sectionKinds.description: 1-3 sentence summary of what a single routine does, in domain language. The long-tail leaf of the documentation tree. Generated with Haiku for utility routines, Sonnet for mid-tier, Opus for headline routines (model tier picked by blast-radius score per ADR-038 §11.0.a).

fields.name: summary
fields.doc: 1-3 sentences, plain prose. No code.

fields.name: inputs
fields.doc: Named inputs in domain terms (not 'INTEGER N' but 'number of policies').

fields.name: outputs
fields.doc: Named outputs in domain terms.

fields.name: sideEffects
fields.doc: Files written, COMMON blocks mutated, IO performed.

fields.name: tier
fields.doc: Picked from migration-plan blast-radius score. Drives model selection.

sectionKinds.label: Data dictionary entry
sectionKinds.description: Per data-item entry: name, type, business meaning, units, valid ranges, where it is read / written. Built from parser COMMON-block output (Phase 5.x parser) plus an LLM pass that infers business meaning + units. The thing Doxygen-style tools never produce.

fields.name: container
fields.doc: COMMON block name, type name, or file name.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: Source-language type (e.g. 'REAL*8', 'INTEGER*4', 'CHARACTER*80'). Verbatim from the parser.

fields.name: businessMeaning
fields.doc: Domain-level description ('customer policy number' not 'unique identifier'). LLM-inferred; SME-confirmed.

fields.name: units
fields.doc: Physical / monetary units ('USD cents', 'metres', 'days since 1970'). LOW confidence by default; SME must promote.

fields.name: readers
fields.doc: Routines that read this item.

fields.name: writers
fields.doc: Routines that write this item.

sectionKinds.label: Glossary term
sectionKinds.description: Domain term in use across the codebase, with definition + source evidence ('POL = policy', 'LOB = line of business'). Bulk-extracted across the whole corpus in one prompt with prompt-caching. Without this, the code reads as gibberish to new engineers.

fields.name: term
fields.doc: The abbreviation / jargon as it appears in the code.

fields.name: definition
fields.doc: Plain-English expansion + meaning.

fields.name: examples
fields.doc: Quoted snippets where the term appears.

sectionKinds.label: External interface entry
sectionKinds.description: Catalogue of every file, JCL DD card, socket, database, MQ queue, COM object, or external service the system touches. Generated from the parser's IO-pattern output (already extracted for Fortran in Phase 5.x) plus an LLM pass that categorises direction + purpose. The external-dependency surface.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Logical name as the customer would refer to it (e.g. 'CUSTOMER_MASTER', 'mainframe billing API', 'audit log file').

fields.name: purpose
fields.doc: Why the system touches this interface, in business terms.

fields.name: format
fields.doc: File format / schema / protocol (e.g. 'fixed-width 240 columns', 'CSV with header', 'JSON over HTTPS').

fields.name: touchpoints
fields.doc: Routines that read or write this interface.

sectionKinds.label: Business rule
sectionKinds.description: Embedded business rule extracted from a conditional or formula in the code. Hybrid extraction mode per ADR-038: conservative by default (only emit when the source has an explicit conditional with clear intent); SME marks rules-dense modules where the aggressive pass runs (every branch becomes a candidate). Confidence field carries the call.

fields.name: ruleText
fields.doc: Plain-English statement of the rule. Use IF…THEN… form when the source is a conditional.

fields.name: category
fields.doc: Business domain (e.g. 'pricing', 'eligibility', 'compliance').

fields.name: extractionMode
fields.doc: Which extraction pass emitted this. Drives default review weight in the UI.

sectionKinds.label: Diagram
sectionKinds.description: Rendered diagram (Mermaid source) for a headline flow or module dependency. Sequence diagrams emit from a single entry routine + call-graph walk; dependency diagrams reuse the existing Phase 8.0.a graph. Picked for the top-N routines by blast-radius score.

fields.name: mermaidSource
fields.doc: Raw Mermaid source. The renderer in the doc-site emits this verbatim.

fields.name: narrative
fields.doc: Optional caption explaining what the diagram shows.
